I understand why some people dislike any AI use, but context matters. ArtRising is a two-person indie team, not a giant publisher with hundreds of employees. According to their Steam disclosure, the game only used AI to refine three decorative paintings and one UI asset, plus grammar corrections for text. They specifically state those assets were not created from scratch by AI and that AI was used as a supporting tool rather than replacing the creative process.

For small indie developers, tools like AI can help save time and money so they can focus on gameplay, programming, design, and polishing the experience. In this case, the game itself, the library design, mechanics, book sorting system, progression, and overall concept were still created by the developers.

It's completely fair to prefer games with no AI involvement at all, but there's also a difference between using AI as a minor production aid and using it to generate the entire game.

I don't really understand the "lazy" argument here. If they were lazy, they wouldn't have spent years developing the other 99% of the game.

ArtRising is a two-person indie team. They designed the gameplay, built the systems, created the world, balanced the puzzles, tested the game, and shipped the product themselves. Using AI to refine a few decorative images or help with grammar doesn't suddenly make them lazy.

By that logic, using Photoshop filters is lazy. Using spellcheck is lazy. Using Unreal Engine instead of writing a custom engine from scratch is lazy. Most creators use tools that save time so they can focus on the parts that matter most.

It's completely fair to dislike AI and choose not to support games that use it. But calling developers lazy because they used a tool for a handful of minor assets while creating an entire game by hand feels like it ignores the thousands of hours of work that went into everything else.

It's a fun game with a lot of heart. They're a small team using the tools they have. And that's what AI is, a tool. Hating the tool is always a pointless endeavor.

We also need to stop lumping in personal/small AI use with the massive corporations that are actually behind the RAM prices, environmental damage, etc. It's the whole shtick of "if consumers don't use one-use plastic, the world will be saved!" while mega-corporations dump waste into the ocean by the megatons.

And before I get that guy who says they're training the AIs of the massive mega-corpos, they're not. 99% of people set up private instances and use only their own machines. No data training outside of their own. It's free, uses only one computer to power itself, and is entirely local.

I am a huge supporter of artists and am very against artists having their work fed into AI without consent and compensation. But the team made it clear they are using THEIR OWN art and have not confirmed that they did anything more than enhance the images.
